newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER SHOWCASE-DORTMUND SUFFER FIRST HOME DEFEAT OF SEASON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-DORTMUND SUFFER FIRST HOME DEFEAT OF SEASON.

text.p: Borussia Dortmund suffered their first home defeat of the German league season on Saturday when they went down 3-1 to lowly Borussia Moenchengladbach after an indisciplined performance by both team and fans.

The German champions put on a poor display in a highly-charged game which saw a player from each side sent off in the first half and an unpleasant incident when frustrated Dortmund fans threw plastic cups on to the pitch and held up a corner.

Just a few days after clinching their place in the semifinals of the European Cup in which they will meet England's Manchester United, Dortmund lacked creativity and bite against a team who are struggling near the bottom of the table.

The reigning Bundesliga champions, who also missed a second-half penalty, lost their place at the top of the table to VfB Stuttgart, who won on Friday, after goals from Swedish striker Martin Dahlin, Pole Andrzej Juskowiak and substitute Jorgen Pettersson exposed huge holes in their defence.
The home side were caught sleeping after just 20 seconds when Dahlin got on the end of a cross from the left from Martin Schneider and headed into the top corner.
When their experienced international defender Juergen Kohler was sent off in the 34th minute for his second bookable offence, Dortmund's hopes of getting out of trouble seemed doomed.
The crowd were angered by the decision and five minutes before halftime Moenchengladbach midfielder Stefan Effenberg was held up from taking a corner when Dortmund fans threw rubbish on to the pitch.
A minute later the visitors were also reduced to 10 men when defender Hubert Fournier was sent off for his second bookable offence.
For a while at the start of the second half Dortmund improved and they won a penalty in the 50th minute when Schneider brought down midfielder Andy Moeller in the box.
But German international Stefan Reuter hit his shot straight at Moenchengladbach keeper Uwe Kamps.
In the 71st minute Juskowiak effectively sealed Moenchengladbach's shock win when he broke clear on the right and slammed the ball into the back of the net.
Dortmund put on the pressure in a tense last period and scored a consolation goal in the 82nd minute when Joerg Heinrich headed in from a corner. A minute later Moeller hit the post.
But a minute from time Pettersson weaved his way past three Dortmund defenders to score a superb individual goal and finish off a miserable day for the champions in front of a capacity 55,000 crowd.

Borussia Dortmund - 1-Stefan Klos, 6-Matthias Sammer, 15-Juergen Kohler, 17-Joerg Heinrich, 14-Paul Lambert (8-Michael Zorc, 66), 16-Martin Kree, 18-Lars Ricken (Knut Reinhardt, 39), 7-Stefan Reuter, 10-Andy Moeller, 9-Stephane Chapuisat, 13-Karlheinz Riedle (11-Heiko Herrlich, 66)

Borussia Moenchengladbach - 1-Uwe Kamps, 27-Stephan Passlack, 4-Patrik Andersson, 21-Hubert Fournier, 13-Martin Schneider, 14-Peter Nielsen (3-Michael Klinkert, 46), 10- Stefan Effenberg, 7-Karlheinz Pflipsen, 8-Peter Wynhoff, 9-Andrzej Juskowiak (26-Joachim Stadler, 86), 30-Martin Dahlin (Jorgen Pettersson, 74).
